questions.questionText: Which quantity can be measured using a ruler?

options.text: the distance travelled by a toy train in one second
the temperature of a toy train
the time taken for a toy train to travel one metre
the volume of a toy train

questions.questionText:
A car is driven from one town to another town along a road that is not straight.
The driver of the car divides the total distance travelled by the total time taken.
Which quantity does the driver calculate?

options.text: the acceleration of the car
the average speed of the car
the kinetic energy of the car
the velocity of the car

questions.questionText: Which quantity can be determined from the area under a speed–time graph?

options.text: acceleration
distance
speed
velocity

questions.questionText:
Samples of three different liquids have equal masses.
The volumes of the samples are 190cm3, 200cm3 and 235cm3.
The liquids are poured into a large measuring cylinder and the liquids form three separate layers
because they do not mix.
What are the readings on the measuring cylinder at the two boundaries between the samples?

options.text: 190cm3 and 390cm3
190cm3 and 425cm3
235cm3 and 425cm3
235cm3 and 435cm3

questions.questionText:
A railway truck of mass 8000kg moves with a velocity of 1.0m/s to the right.
It collides with a railway truck of mass 12000kg moving at 2.0m/s to the left.
The two trucks become joined to each other when they collide and move off together.
What is the velocity of the two trucks after the collision?

options.text: 1.6m/s to the left
0.80m/s to the left
0.80m/s to the right
1.6m/s to the right

questions.questionText:
Which row describes the particle structure of a gas?
distance between motion of
the particles the particles

options.text: close together vibrating
close together random
far apart vibrating
far apart random

questions.questionText:
The particles of a gas in a container of fixed volume gain energy in the kinetic store.
Which effect does this have on the gas?

options.text: Both the pressure and the temperature of the gas increase.
Only the temperature of the gas increases.
Neither the pressure nor the temperature of the gas increases.
Only the pressure of the gas increases.

questions.questionText:
Gas particles exert a pressure when they collide with the walls of a container.
Which statement about the gas particles is correct?

options.text: They experience a change in force, which results in a pressure equal to momentum  area. momentum
They experience a change in force, which results in a pressure equal to . area
They experience a change in momentum, which results in a pressure equal to force  area. force
They experience a change in momentum, which results in a pressure equal to . area

questions.questionText:
A solid changes into a liquid.
Which term describes this change in state?

options.text: boiling
condensation
freezing
melting

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows some of the apparatus used to determine the specific heat capacity of a
metal block.
thermometer
metal block
Which additional pieces of apparatus are required to find the specific heat capacity?

options.text: stop-watch, voltmeter and balance
resistor, stop-watch and ruler
ruler, balance and force meter
voltmeter, thermistor and insulation

questions.questionText:
Four different surfaces are at the same high temperature.
Which surface emits thermal radiation at the slowest rate?
colour of texture of
surface area/cm2
surface surface

options.text: black dull 10
black dull 100
white shiny 10
white shiny 100

questions.questionText:
An object has a constant temperature.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: There is no energy transfer to or from the object.
The rate at which the object receives energy is the same as the rate at which it transfers energy away.
The rate at which the object receives energy is smaller than the rate at which it transfers energy away.
The rate at which the object receives energy is greater than the rate at which it transfers energy away.

questions.questionText:
Which row correctly describes light waves?
wave type direction of vibration

options.text: longitudinal parallel to direction of wave travel
longitudinal perpendicular to direction of wave travel
transverse parallel to direction of wave travel
transverse perpendicular to direction of wave travel

questions.questionText:
A narrow beam of light consists of two waves of different wavelengths.
The beam of light hits a sharp edge.
Which effect will be seen beyond the sharp edge?

options.text: Both waves continue along the same straight line as before.
Both waves bend sharply and continue along a new straight line.
The wave of longer wavelength bends round the sharp edge more than the wave of shorter wavelength.
The wave of shorter wavelength bends round the sharp edge more than the wave of longer wavelength.

questions.questionText:
An object is placed 30cm in front of a plane mirror.
Which statement describes the image of the object?

options.text: The image is the same size as the object and 30cm from the object.
The image is the same size as the object and 60cm from the object.
The image is smaller than the object and 30cm from the object.
The image is smaller than the object and 60cm from the object.

questions.questionText: Which statement about total internal reflection at a glass–air boundary is correct?

options.text: The angle of incidence inside the glass must be equal to the critical angle.
The angle of incidence inside the glass must be less than the critical angle.
The critical angle is proportional to the refractive index of the glass.
The speed of light in glass must be less than the speed of light in air.

questions.questionText:
What is the speed of radio waves in a vacuum and what is the speed of gamma rays in a
vacuum?
speed of radio waves speed of gamma rays

options.text: less than 3.0  108m/s less than 3.0  108m/s
less than 3.0  108m/s more than 3.0  108m/s
more than 3.0  108m/s more than 3.0  108m/s

questions.questionText: What is a compression?

options.text: a point in a longitudinal wave where the particles of the medium are close together
a point in a longitudinal wave where the particles of the medium are far apart
a point in a transverse wave where the particles of the medium are close together
a point in a transverse wave where the particles of the medium are far apart

questions.questionText:
Which row describes the magnetic field around a weak magnet?
direction of field spacing of field lines

options.text: north pole to south pole close together
north pole to south pole far apart
south pole to north pole close together
south pole to north pole far apart

questions.questionText: What is the electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a cell?

options.text: the charge that passes through the cell per unit time
the energy supplied per unit charge as charge passes through the cell
the total charge flowing through the cell
the total energy stored in the cell

questions.questionText:
In which mains electric wires are the fuse and the switch placed?
fuse switch

options.text: earth live
live live
live neutral
neutral neutral

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the split-ring commutator in an electric motor?

options.text: to ensure that the magnetic field in the motor changes direction every half rotation
to ensure that the magnetic field in the motor stays in the same direction at all times
to ensure that the turning effect on the motor changes direction every half rotation
to ensure that the turning effect on the motor stays in the same direction at all times

questions.questionText:
A beta particle has less mass than an alpha particle, but the speed of a beta particle emitted
during radioactive decay is approximately 20 times greater than the speed of an alpha particle.
Which statement correctly compares properties of these two particles?

options.text: Alpha particles are less penetrating because they have less kinetic energy than beta particles.
Alpha particles are more penetrating because they have less kinetic energy than beta particles.
Alpha particles are less ionising because they have more kinetic energy than beta particles.
Alpha particles are more ionising because they have more kinetic energy than beta particles.

questions.questionText: Which observation provides evidence for the nuclear atom?

options.text: attraction of opposite charges
emission of -rays during the decay of a radioactive nuclide
scattering of -particles by a thin metal foil
scattering of -rays by a thin metal foil

questions.questionText: Which effect on living things is not caused by ionising radiation?

options.text: cancer
cell death
infection
mutation

questions.questionText:
Isotope X is radioactive.
Which statement about X must be correct?

options.text: A nucleus of X is unstable.
X emits -particles.
X emits -particles.
X emits -radiation.

questions.questionText:
An experiment is done to measure the radiation from a radioactive source. The source has a
half-life of 10 minutes.
The source is placed close to a detector that is connected to a counter, as shown.
radioactive
counter
detector source
The average background count rate is 20 counts/minute.
At the start of the experiment, the count rate recorded by the counter is 1000 counts/minute.
What is the count rate 10 minutes later?

options.text: 490 counts/minute
500 counts/minute
510 counts/minute
530 counts/minute

questions.questionText: In which direction does the Sun appear to move every day, when viewed from the Earth?

options.text: east to west
north to south
south to north
west to east

questions.questionText:
The orbit of Mercury is closer to the Sun than the orbit of the Earth is to the Sun.
How do the values of the gravitational field strength of the Sun near Mercury and the orbital
speed of Mercury compare to those values for the Earth?
gravitational field
orbital speed
strength of the Sun
of Mercury
near Mercury

greater slower
